body.statement: There is a universal \(C>0\) such that \(\mathsf A(G,T,e,\delta)\) first determines whether \(d_e(G)<\infty\). On the finite branch it returns exactly \((d_e(G),p_e,\mathcal Q_{G,e},h_{G,e})\), where \(p_e\in K_G[t]\) is monic with rational-circuit coefficients. On the transcendental branch it returns exactly \((\infty,\mathcal N_{G,e})\), where \(\mathcal N_{G,e}\) certifies that the queried-coordinate projection of a positive-dimensional irreducible generic-fiber component is dominant onto \(\mathbb A^1_{K_G}\), and it returns no \(p_e\), \(\mathcal Q_{G,e}\), or \(h_{G,e}\). In \(\mathsf{ArithmeticModel}\), construction time and certificate length are at most \(n^{C(k+1)}\operatorname{poly}(\log(1/\delta))\), and total symbolic error probability is at most \(\delta\). On the tree-plus-\(k\) class, the finite branch strictly strengthens the general polynomial-space yes-or-no procedure by returning the coordinate degree and eliminant.
body.justification: A sharp degree frontier becomes operational only with a complete graph-input certificate of the queried minimal polynomial.
body.gap: Hollering, Misra, and Sturma search bounded-degree rational formulas, and Dörfler et al. decide general identification in polynomial space; neither returns algebraic coordinate minimal polynomials with fixed-parameter certificates.
body.consumer: fasttreeid can replace its \(0/1/2\) status by exact higher finite degree and a verifiable branch polynomial for added-parent graphs.
